Subject: PrivGPU: warmup/eviction policy and throughput handoff

Hi Sanjeev / ACME infra,

Following our kickoff earlier this week I wanted to align on two tightly-coupled items before the 4/19 capacity test: (1) warmup/eviction expectations for your private GPU pool, and (2) our throughput handoff for the initial SLA enrollment. We attached a small throughput matrix and a draft warmup/eviction policy for reference.

Quick context: Redwood's allocator assumes a warm pool target (ready GPUs) sized to absorb a 3x burst relative to steady runrate with a 10s cold-start amortization window for KV cache. If your workload has long-prefix reuse (chat sessions), warmup is much cheaper; if it's stateless single-shot generation, warmup + cache pressure drives different sizing.

Ask for ACME: can you confirm a realistic sustained qps (tokens/sec) and peak burst multiplier for week-of-4/19? We will map those numbers to the matrix and recommend slab sizes and eviction thresholds.

If helpful, Jonas can propose a concrete slab/count target and a basic rollback plan (eviction aggressiveness, NIC oversubscription guardrails).

Thanks,
Soojin

Thanks Soojin — good summary. A few clarifications from our side:
- Sustained: 120 concurrent requests (avg 12 tokens/sec per request) -> ~1,440 tokens/sec steady-state.
- Peak: we see spikes up to 6x during business-hours promos (last spike lasted ~8 minutes).
- Workload: mostly short chat sessions (20-60 tokens average) but a 10% tail of long transcription jobs (2k-10k tokens). Those heavy requests are isolated to a separate tenant but share the same NICs.

We want warmup to avoid tail latency regressions but are sensitive to egress costs on staging. Let us know how much reserved warm pool you recommend and what to watch for during the test.

— Sanjeev

Subject: Re: PrivGPU: warmup/eviction policy and throughput handoff

Thanks Sanjeev — that profile is helpful. I ran the attached throughput matrix against our slab model and here's a short recommendation:

- Steady mapping: 1,440 tokens/sec -> baseline of 4 medium slabs (each slab = 8 A100-equivalent GPUs, ~200 tokens/sec effective throughput with batching and KV cache for chat). That gives headroom for steady-state concurrent sessions and auto-batching.
- Burst sizing: 6x peak -> target warm pool = 8 slabs pre-warmed (grow from 4 -> 8 under canary ramp). This uses a 2x buffer above observed peak to account for model variance and QoS smoothing.
- Eviction policy: aggressive eviction after 60s idle for long-one-off tenants; soft eviction for chat tenants (300s) to preserve KV. Evict order: least-recently-used slab; do not evict if slab still has >10 active KV sessions.
- NIC guidance: keep NIC oversubscription <= 1.6x for steady load; do not exceed 2.2x during bursts. If egress approaches 85% link utilization, trigger admission control for transcription jobs.
- Rollback plan: if 95th latency breaches SLA during the ramp, immediately reduce target warm pool by 25% and redirect transcription jobs to the secondary carveout.

I'll attach a small table mapping these numbers to the workbook. We should also run a targeted 30-minute spike test that replicates the 6x multiplier with a 10% long-job tail.

Jonas
Senior Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference

Adding ops runbook items so the test is actionable:

1) Pre-test checklist (to run 30m before ramp)
   - Validate NIC baseline utilization and BGP session health on each rack.
   - Confirm slab images have the tuned kernel (nvfuser tuned) and quantization profile.
   - Push warm pool pre-warm RPC to allocated slabs (Jonas will provide IDs).

2) During ramp (onsite/remote roles)
   - Ops lead: monitor 95th/99th latencies, GPU utilization, device memory pressure, and KV hit-rate.
   - If KV hit-rate drops below 60% and 95th latency > SLA: initiate graceful admission (throttle new chat sessions) and increase slab warm pool by +1 immediately if NIC < 75%.
   - If NIC > 85%: pause long transcription jobs and signal ACME infra to add NIC capacity or shift transcription to the carveout.

3) Post-test postmortem anchors
   - Capture sample traces for requests that hit >2s token processing.
   - Snapshot cache sizes and eviction counts.
   - Collect egress billing delta estimate.

I'll be on the call for the 4/19 test window. David, can you prepare a small dashboard (token throughput, slab counts, NIC %) and share the link?

- Grace
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
